Phone call script (you can read this almost verbatim):

“Hi, I’m in Fort Worth, ZIP 76102, and I need a plumber for an urgent leaking sink. When the water’s on, it’s a steady leak into the cabinet underneath, and after I turn the faucet off it keeps dripping more slowly. The cabinet is getting wet, so I’ve been trying not to use the sink much.

I’m looking for an emergency or priority appointment as soon as possible, ideally today or tomorrow.

Could you tell me:
- What’s your earliest availability today or tomorrow, and what arrival window you offer?
- What’s your service call or diagnostic fee, and what does it include?
- What’s your hourly rate, and is there any emergency or after-hours surcharge?
- Are you licensed and insured, and do you offer any warranty on this kind of repair?
- Roughly what price range I might expect for a typical leaking-sink repair, assuming nothing major needs replacement?”

Key things to ask every plumber:
- Earliest time they can come (today vs tomorrow) and arrival window.  
- Service/diagnostic fee and whether it’s applied to the repair if you go ahead.  
- Hourly rate and any emergency/after-hours surcharge.  
- License/insurance status; whether they warranty parts and labor.  
- How payment works (card vs cash, on-site vs invoice).

Until they arrive:
- Put a bowl/pan or tray under the leak and swap out any soaked towels so the cabinet doesn’t swell or mold.  
- Keep the sink use to a minimum; if the shutoff valves under the sink work, turn them off when you’re not actively running water.  
- Remove any items from the cabinet that could be damaged by moisture (paper goods, cleaners in cardboard boxes, etc.).

If you tell me whether it’s a kitchen or bathroom sink and your preferred time windows (e.g., “anytime today after 4 pm,” “tomorrow morning only”), I can tailor the wording further. </action>
